title: Microsoft Teams: report suspicious guest invitations to your admin
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly says Microsoft Learn does not state a role that can view the security submissions report. Microsoft's Teams administrator role reference explicitly grants Teams Administrators access to all reports in the Teams admin center. The roadmap facts, notice, documented controls and qualified licensing gaps otherwise check out.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let Teams users report suspicious invitations to join another organisation as a guest to their IT admin.
claims.quote: When users receive an unexpected or potentially malicious invitation to join another organization as a guest, they can report it to their IT admin for review

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Messaging policies > policy > Report a security concern is a documented path, with Settings & policies noted for the new experience.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Messaging policies. ... Select a policy. ... Turn on the setting: Report a security concern. ... To access this policy in the new experience, go to Settings & policies.

claims.claim: The MicrosoftTeams module documents Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity <policy> -AllowSecurityEndUserReporting $true for enabling security-concern reporting, with guest-invitation applicability explicitly unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy ... [[-Identity] <XdsIdentity>] ... [-AllowSecurityEndUserReporting <Boolean>] ... This setting determines if users can report any security concern posted in message to their admin. Possible values: True, False

claims.claim: AllowSecurityEndUserReporting is Boolean and $false disables the setting.
claims.quote: This setting determines if users can report any security concern posted in message to their admin. Possible values: True, False ... Type: | Boolean

claims.claim: The report is reached through Teams admin center > Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports > User reported security submissions.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Analytics & reports > Protection reports. ... On the View reports tab, under Report, select User reported security submissions.

claims.claim: No API for the Teams admin center User reported security submissions report is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams User reported security submissions report API Microsoft Graph permissions role view report; "User reported security submissions" permissions role API PowerShell. Opened the report page and submissions-teams; no API for this report found.

claims.where: controls[2]; Governance controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: No separate UI or automation switch for guest-invitation reporting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams report suspicious guest invitations Report a security concern separate policy PowerShell guest invitation reporting; "guest invitations" "report" "Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy". Read end-user-reporting-security and the cmdlet reference; none found.

claims.claim: The governing Teams reporting setting is on by default, so guest-invitation reporting arrives without admin action where that setting remains enabled.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center: 'On' by default and controls whether users are able to report messages and user from Teams.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the reporting outcome presented to the guest-invitation reporter.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The notice describes a user-initiated report and describes no autonomous action.
claims.quote: Users can report suspicious guest invitations when declining them in Teams. Reports are shared with their IT admin through the User reported security submissions report in the Teams admin center and with Microsoft for review.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: The report documentation lists Calling, Chats and channels, and User categories, without a guest-invitation category.
claims.quote: Under Report category, choose one of the following categories: Calling; Chats and channels; User

claims.claim: The report page lists reporting settings as prerequisites and names no licence in those prerequisites.
claims.quote: Users can submit reports only when the required reporting settings are enabled in the Teams admin center. ... For chat and channel messages and external users, the Report a security concern setting must be turned on in the user's messaging policy.

claims.claim: The Teams security-reporting and messaging-policy pages name Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Microsoft Defender XDR for malicious-message reporting.
claims.quote: Report a security concern - When this is ON, users can report malicious messages in Microsoft Teams in organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Microsoft Defender XDR.

claims.claim: The Defender reporting page instead names Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2, or Microsoft Defender XDR.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2, or Microsoft Defender XDR, admins can decide whether users can report messages, calls, meetings, or meeting participants in Microsoft Teams.

claims.where: Scope; controls[0].scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Custom messaging policies can be assigned to users, allowing the reporting setting to differ between users.
claims.quote: Users in your organization will automatically get the global policy, unless you create and assign a custom policy. Edit the settings in the global policy or create and assign one or more custom policies to turn on or turn off the features that you want.

claims.claim: A second Defender portal setting must be on for user-reported messages to appear correctly on the Submissions page.
claims.quote: If "Report a security concern" is turned on in the Teams admin center, it also needs to be turned on in the Defender portal for user reported messages to show up correctly on the User reported tab on the Submissions page.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn says user reporting of external users is not yet supported in Microsoft Defender.
claims.quote: User reporting of external users is not yet supported in Microsoft Defender.

claims.claim: Learn has not confirmed that the documented PowerShell reporting parameter governs guest-invitation reporting.
claims.quote: Searched: "guest invitations" "report" "Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy". Read Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy, including AllowSecurityEndUserReporting, and end-user-reporting-security; the parameter describes security concerns posted in messages, without naming guest invitations.

claims.claim: Microsoft names Teams Administrator or Global Administrator for configuring user reporting in the Teams admin center and advises least privilege.
claims.quote: To view or configure user reporting in the Teams admin center, you need to be a member of the Global Administrator or Teams Administrator roles. ... Microsoft strongly advocates for the principle of least privilege.

claims.claim: Learn does not state the role needed to view the User reported security submissions report.
claims.quote: Teams Administrator ... Everything in the Microsoft Teams admin center and associated PowerShell controls, including: ... Access all reports in the Microsoft Teams admin center
claims.fix: Replace the final sentence with: 'Microsoft documents that Teams Administrators can access all reports in the Teams admin center.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/using-admin-roles. This states a documented sufficient role without claiming it is the only role permitted.
